note: On profile and psychology he is the closest thing in this batch to the stated ICP, and on the good-to-great criterion he is its purest expression — 'I would say I'm in above average shape, but I've always wanted to be in like tremendous shape' and 'the quality of my life is not horrible by any means. I just know what it can be.' He holds a professional management role, running the turf and a crew of about 20 at a private golf club, which sits close enough to the 'or equivalent' clause to count, and he is emphatically not deconditioned: climbing two to four times a week, a former runner who lost 50-60 lb unaided. Health has softened rather than collapsed, which is exactly the severity the criterion describes. He fails on income alone, and not on willingness — he had priced the offer at around $6,000 before hearing it and read the number as a value signal. He failed on liquidity: one credit card with a $2,000 limit, two lenders declining live, $2,500 still owed to midwives and a baby due in August. This is the sharpest test yet of the observation already recorded in icp.json that income screening may be filtering out deals a payment plan could carry. Here the ICP would have kept him and the payment plan still could not carry him.
